answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make each new identity earn its haven through a voyage of time-locked work: for 30 epochs its rewards stay escrowed while verifiers drawn at random from an unrelated grove of peers spot-check its outputs, and any failed check burns the escrow. An attacker running 1,000 fake agents must fund and genuinely perform 1,000 parallel workloads for a month with nothing withdrawable, so every sybil costs about as much as an honest agent and earns no edge.
